domain: Indian Criminal Law - NDPS, BNS, BNSS, BSA, Limitation Act, Police Manuals
description: Graph-native ontology for a NARIT-AI-style legal investigation system. Models statutes, sections, cases, doctrines, procedures, police manuals, FIRs, and defence arguments with explicit relational structure to enable multi-hop legal reasoning.

Section.description: A specific numbered provision within a statute

Case.description: A judicial decision (Supreme Court, High Court, or lower court)

properties.court: string (Supreme Court | High Court | Sessions | Magistrate)

Doctrine.description: A legal principle, test, or interpretive rule established or applied by courts

Procedure.description: A statutory or judicially mandated procedural step

PoliceManual.description: A state or central police regulation or manual provision

FIR.description: A First Information Report node representing an active investigation

DefenceArgument.description: A defence strategy or argument raised in past cases

MAPS_TO.description: Cross-statute provision mapping (e.g., IPC S420 -> BNS S318)

DECIDED_UNDER.description: The primary statutory hook the case was decided under

INTERPRETS.description: The case provides an authoritative reading of the provision

ESTABLISHES.description: The case lays down the doctrine or test

APPLIES.description: The case applies an existing doctrine

CONSTRAINS.description: A judgment lays down binding guidelines on police procedure

CONSTRAINS_PROCEDURE.description: A judgment imposes judicial requirements on a procedural step

IMPLEMENTS.description: The manual operationalizes a statutory provision

OVERRULES.description: The case overrules an earlier decision

REQUIRES.description: The procedural step is mandated by a statutory section

TRIGGERS.description: The FIR activates a mandatory procedural sequence

CHARGED_UNDER.description: The FIR invokes a specific statutory offence

RAISES.description: The case records a defence argument being raised

REBUTS.description: The case provides a judicial rebuttal to a defence argument

indexes: CREATE INDEX statute_name IF NOT EXISTS FOR (s:Statute) ON (s.name)
CREATE INDEX section_id IF NOT EXISTS FOR (s:Section) ON (s.id)
CREATE INDEX case_citation IF NOT EXISTS FOR (c:Case) ON (c.citation)
CREATE INDEX doctrine_name IF NOT EXISTS FOR (d:Doctrine) ON (d.name)
CREATE INDEX fir_number IF NOT EXISTS FOR (f:FIR) ON (f.fir_number)
